cf.title: Avoid O(N^3) planning time in choose_plan_name()

input.subject: O(N^3) planning time in choose_plan_name() since 8c49a484e8e

verdict_reasoning: Nothing that survived questions the goal or the design. The patch fixes a planning-time regression from 8c49a484e8e, and v6 implements the threshold hash table that Robert Haas proposed. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, asks for a lasting regression test that crosses the 32-name threshold, which is a fixable point. A committer who knows the planner must still decide on v6 and on whether it goes into REL_19_STABLE.

brief.title: Avoid O(N^3) planning time in choose_plan_name()
brief.problem: Since commit 8c49a484e8e, choose_plan_name() tries suffixes 1, 2, 3, ... and scans every assigned name for each try, so planning is O(N^3) in subplans sharing a base name. A 4000-arm UNION plans in about 17 s on master against about 19 ms on v18. The author says only generated SQL hits this: many UNION arms, scalar sublinks or ORed IN subqueries.
brief.proposed_design: v6 keeps the existing list and, once a statement has 32 subplan names, also puts them in a simplehash keyed by the C string. Each entry records whether the exact name is taken and the suffix where the search for a free name_N starts. Below 32 names the code runs as before, and the chosen names do not change.
author_claims: v6 plans a 4000-arm UNION in about 22 ms, against 16.6 s on master and 19 ms on 18.6.
4000 CTEs with different names plan in 126 ms with v6, against 153 ms on master and 128 ms on 18.6.
Generated names are byte-identical to master's in regression tests, four contrib suites and 32 collision statements.
Small statements plan 2-4% slower with default builds, but equal with -falign-functions=64, so the author attributes the gap to code layout.
Keeping today's names matters because users write them into pg_plan_advice strings, and pg_plan_advice ships in 19.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund and Tom Lane questioned the complexity and suggested a single counter; Tom found v3 hard to reason about. Robert Haas proposed the threshold hash table that v6 implements, and later asked why the UNION case is so much worse, which the author answered; no one has reviewed v6 yet.
unclear: No reviewer has said whether v6 should go into REL_19_STABLE before 19.0 or wait for master.
The material does not say whether the 32-name threshold, borrowed from ec_derives_hash, suits this workload beyond the author's microbenchmark.
No one has measured planner memory for v6 once the hash table is built.
Tom and Robert left open whether 19 should change the naming scheme to a single counter before release.

objections.title: Two lookup paths must agree, and only rare statements use the hash
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a subplan kind or changes the naming rule, and updates the list search but not the hash entries. The regression suite has only small statements, so it stays green. A user whose generated SQL passes 32 names finds that their pg_plan_advice strings now point at different subplans.
objections.argument: v6 keeps the list and adds a simplehash above 32 names, so two structures must give the same name for every input (message #15). The author checked this with the threshold set to 0, but as a one-time run, and the prose does not say the suite keeps doing so. Names matter because advice strings refer to them (messages #12, #14). The list of touched files shows only subselect.sql, with no statement known to cross the threshold.
objections.author_must_show: Which regression test crosses the 32-name threshold with mixed generated and user-written names, so that a future change to one path alone fails the suite?

critic.reasoning: The two-path design copies ec_derives_hash and Robert Haas proposed it, so the design stands. But the visible prose names no subselect.sql statement that passes 32 names, and the threshold-0 check was a one-time run, so a later divergence in choose_plan_name() could pass the suite.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds fields to PlannerGlobal in src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h, which extensions that include that header see.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: choose_plan_name() in planner.c changes how it finds a free subplan name; the author reports the chosen names stay the same.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The regression is in 19 and no reviewer has said whether v6 goes into REL_19_STABLE before 19.0.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The list search and the hash table must give the same name for every input from now on.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Every statement with subplans calls choose_plan_name(); measurements.txt shows 2-4% slower small statements with default builds, equal with aligned builds.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which regression test crosses the 32-name threshold with mixed generated and user-written names, so that a later change to one lookup path alone fails the suite?
Is v6 meant for REL_19_STABLE before 19.0, or for master only?
How much planner memory does the hash table use for a statement with 4000 subplan names, compared with master?
Does the 32-name threshold hold for statements that mix generated and user-written names, beyond the two pure cases in measurements.txt section 3?
Should 19 keep the smallest-free-suffix naming, or switch to a single counter before release, given that pg_plan_advice strings refer to these names?

committability.owner_note: Robert Haas proposed the threshold hash table that v6 implements, and Tom Lane and Andres Freund commented on earlier versions. No one has reviewed v6 yet.
committability.liability: The owner signs for subplan names staying identical between the list path and the hash path, for as long as pg_plan_advice strings refer to those names.
committability.author_follow_up: The author produced six versions and detailed measurements in about four weeks, and answered reviewers' questions in the thread.

priority.reason: Only generated SQL with many same-named subplans hits the problem, but it is a regression from v18 of up to about 1000 times in planning time. The patch is 14.2 KB, mostly in planner.c, and reuses the simplehash threshold pattern of ec_derives_hash.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody could check that the hash path and the list path choose the same name in every collision case, or that v6 never truncates its keys. The memory use of the hash table is also unmeasured.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: allow partial union-all and improve parallel subquery costing
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build partial paths for UNION ALL so the branches can run under a parallel plan. It also changes subquery costing to account for parallelism, with a regression test and before/after plans for TPC-DS query 5.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took up the patch during the commitfests. In March 2021 the patch no longer applied, and the entry was set to Waiting for Author. The author sent no rebased patch, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Since no new patch has been provided, marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: add explicit partial union-all and improve parallel subquery costing
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build partial Append paths for UNION ALL subqueries so their branches can run in parallel. It also changes subquery scan costing to take parallel workers into account in the row estimate.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after Ronan Dunklau's review asked for a regression test of the new partial append path and questioned the subquery scan row estimate change. Daniel Gustafsson closed the entry because the thread stalled with these requests unanswered. An earlier round was also closed after the patch needed a rebase and no new version came in time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
With the thread stalled and requests for a test (documentation really?) not
responded to I'm marking this patch Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert commit 66c0185a3 and follow-on patches.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert commit 66c0185a3 and follow-on patches.
Reverted commit(s): Allow planner to use Merge Append to efficiently implement UNION; Fix assert failure when planning setop subqueries with CTEs; Don't zero tuple_fraction when planning UNIONs with ORDER BYs; Don't adjust ressortgroupref in generate_setop_child_grouplist(); Finish incomplete revert of ec63622c0.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts 66c0185a3 (Allow planner to use Merge Append to
efficiently implement UNION) as well as the follow-on commits
d5d2205c8, 3b1a7eb28, 7487044d6.  In addition to those, 07746a8ef
had to be removed then re-applied in a different place, because
66c0185a3 moved the relevant code.

The reason for this last-minute thrashing is that depesz found a
case in which the patched code creates a completely wrong plan
that silently gives incorrect query results.  It's unclear what
the cause is or how many cases are affected, but with beta1 wrap
staring us in the face, there's no time for closer investigation.
After we figure that out, we can decide whether to un-revert this
for beta2 or hold it for v18.

(also some private discussion among pgsql-release)

precedents_retrieved.title: quick and dirty fix: Quadratic planning time for ordered paths over partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Aleksander Alekseev
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch caches the position of the last found equivalence member in a static variable in find_ec_member_matching_pathkeys(), so lookups done in partition order take constant time. It was offered as a stopgap for planning time that grows quadratically with the number of partitions, until Yuya Watari's larger equivalence class refactoring lands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that one static cache shared by all equivalence classes helps only one call pattern, which unrelated changes could break, and that integer division with a variable divisor may make things slower. He said the fix belongs at a higher level. Alvaro Herrera and Aleksander Alekseev pointed the author to Watari's patch series instead, and Herrera showed it cuts planning time for the same test from about 2700 ms to 600 ms.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
That "quick fix" seems extremely horrid: since there's only one static
cache variable for all ECs, it's going to help only one very specific
call pattern, which could easily get broken by unrelated changes.

precedents_retrieved.title: Subplan result cache
precedents_retrieved.summary: Heikki Linnakangas proposed caching SubPlan results inside nodeSubplan.c, keyed by the correlation parameters, so a correlated subquery runs once per distinct parameter set. On TPC-DS query 6 this cut runtime from about 30 s to 120 ms.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer, David Rowley, asked for the cache to be a separate plan node, similar to Materialize, that the planner adds based on cost and that could also serve parameterized nested loops. He set the patch to waiting on author, but no new version followed, so Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback because the status had not changed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
From looking at the code I see that the caching is being done inside
nodeSubplan.c. I don't think this is the right approach to the
problem.

precedents_retrieved.title: Consider parallel for LATERAL subqueries having LIMIT/OFFSET
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes set_rel_consider_parallel so that a lateral subquery with LIMIT/OFFSET may still be considered for parallel query, so a Gather can go above the whole nested loop. A later version allows this only when rel->lateral_relids is not empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author argued that each outer row gets its own execution of the limited subquery, but Tom Lane (seen only in quoted text) and Robert Haas were not convinced this is safe. Tom Lane noted that the patch took any lateral dependency as enough, even one that does not feed the limited subquery. Robert Haas said the real issue is where parameters are set and used, which the LATERAL keyword does not capture. The commitfest manager returned it because no further review was coming, and asked for a more rigorous correctness argument or simpler constraints.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The problem here isn't created by LATERAL, but by parameters.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve planner cost estimations for alternative subplans
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Melanie Plageman, Tomas Vondra, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes how the planner costs an AlternativeSubPlan (hashed or per-row lookup) for the rest of the query. It replaces the use of the per-row estimate with a heuristic blend of the two alternatives' costs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said that averaging the costs of two alternatives is wrong in principle, because at run time the executor uses one of them. Tomas Vondra expected regressions where the first plan is used, and the author then found queries that ran slower with the patch. The author suggested moving to Tom Lane's approach of passing a number-of-evaluations estimate to cost_qual_eval, or to Andy Fan's proof of concept that picks the SubPlan during planning, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that averaging together the costs of the alternatives seems
wrong in principle.  It's going to be one or the other, not some
quantum-mechanical superposition.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove dead macro exec_subplan_get_plan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the macro exec_subplan_get_plan, which no code uses anymore. Richard Guo suggested using the similar macro planner_subplan_get_plan where code now fetches subplans by hand.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane asked whether the PlannedStmt->subplans list was still needed or whether the accessors should use the macro again; the author showed that the list is still used. Nobody pursued the patch after September 2022, so the commitfest manager marked it rejected. He judged that removing unused macros is not worth the effort unless it is part of a larger patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think the conclusion here was that the actual list is still used and
cleaning up unused macros isn't worth the hassle unless it's part of
some larger patch?

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallelize correlated subqueries that execute within each worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build parallel plans for queries with correlated subplans when each subplan runs entirely within one parallel worker, so no Param value has to pass between workers. After review, the design changed to treat PARAM_EXEC params as parallel safe by default, track required params on each rel, and insert a Gather node only where that set is empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread shows no author reply after Tomas Vondra's July 2024 review, and the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024. That review found that regression tests failed on a changed plan in select_parallel, reported a compiler warning, and listed code comments. It also said no reviewer was able to confirm that the PARAM handling is correct.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And in general the patch looks reasonably simple and clean, but my knowledge of PARAM intricacies is pretty much nil, so I'm hesitant to claim the patch is correct.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P4] was rejected because one static cache helped a single call pattern, but v6 uses a per-statement hash table that also covers different user-given names, as Robert asked in message #14. Message #8 refers to an earlier idea from Heikki that is not in the material, and message #12 reports it is not in this thread either.

The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump content or psql change, and v6 keeps master's subplan names byte-identical, so pg_plan_advice strings and EXPLAIN output stay the same. The one open contract question is whether 19 should switch naming schemes before release (messages #8, #12); that choice exists with or without this patch, and this patch does not decide it.

The patch adds no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk, WAL, catalog or protocol change. It adds a planner-local hash table and fields to PlannerGlobal in pathnodes.h, which are not ABI concerns before 19.0, and the chosen names stay the same, so stored pg_plan_advice strings keep matching.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes how the planner picks internal subplan names, adds no new object, setting, function or privilege, and keeps the names users see in EXPLAIN and pg_plan_advice unchanged. On denial of service, it removes an existing problem: today any user who can send a query can make a backend spend seconds of CPU in choose_plan_name() with a few thousand UNION arms, and v6 brings that back to v18 levels. The hash table grows with the number of subplans, so its size follows the length of the query text. v1 could loop forever in a non-assert build, ignoring cancel, when C code set aliases longer than NAMEDATALEN (message #5). v6 keys the table by the full C string, which removes that cause. Without the code I could not check that v6 never truncates or bounds its keys.

The design is the one Robert Haas proposed in message #14, it fixes a regression from 8c49a484e8e, and it costs nothing measurable below the threshold. [P4] does not apply: this is the general fix it asked for. The single objection asks for a lasting test, not a different design.

No existing feature, setting or extension avoids this cost. The slowdown is inside choose_plan_name(), which every statement with subplans calls, so users cannot work around it and an extension cannot replace it. v6 reuses simplehash with a 32-name threshold, the pattern ec_derives_hash in equivclass.c already uses, so it adds no new mechanism. [P4] concerned a static cache shared by all equivalence classes and does not apply.

The demand case holds because this fixes a planning-time regression from v18, in code new in 19. Generated SQL with a few hundred UNION arms or sublinks that plans in milliseconds on 18 would plan 2x to 1000x slower after upgrade (message #5, measurements.txt). No field report is shown, but one independent developer hit it during other planner work (message #2). Robert Haas, who wrote the code, accepted fixing it and proposed the v6 design (message #14). The cost falls only on statements with 32 or more subplan names.
